items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to mobility vehicles and new mobility vehicles
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5765

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to mobility vehicles and new mobility vehicles

PURPOSE OF THE BILL: To amend the Vehicle and Traffic Law (VTL) to
authorize mobility dealers to display, advertise, store and/or
demonstrate new motor vehicles modified to accommodate persons with
disabilities.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS: The bill amends several provisions of
VTL § 415 to authorize motor vehicle dealers specializing in motor
vehicles that have been specially converted and equipped to transport
a person with disabilities to display, advertise, store and/or
demonstrate new mobility vehicles.

Section 1 of the bill makes amendments to the "definition" provisions
of VTL § 415(1), including new definitions for "new motor vehicle" and
"mobility vehicle" to provide the terms and conditions for
demonstration, display and sale of vehicles that have been specially
converted and equipped to transport a person with a disability.

Section 2 of the bill adds a new paragraph c-1 to subdivision 7 of
section 415 to:

(1) Require that any dealer engaged in displaying and demonstrating
mobility vehicles shall notify prospective purchasers regarding the
warranty on the mobility modifications and the impact, if any of the
modifications on the warranty of the underlying vehicle; and

(2) Authorize a motor vehicle dealer engaged in displaying and
demonstrating mobility vehicles to perform repairs on modifications,
but prohibits repair work on the original manufactured portion of the
vehicle unless licensed to do so pursuant to Article 12-A of the VTL.

Finally, the legislation does not interfere with any existing dealer
rights under the Vehicle and Traffic law. As such, the legislation
does not impair any dealer from selling a used mobility vehicle to a
consumer, nor does it prohibit a new motor vehicle dealer from
engaging in the sale of new mobility vehicles in accordance with his
or her certificate of registration.

JUSTIFICATION: In the past, a driver with physical disabilities or a
person wishing to purchase a vehicle that can accommodate equipment
for secure ingress, transportation, and egress of persons requiring a
wheelchair or scooter would need to purchase a motor vehicle and then
have the post-sale modifications made to the vehicle by an appropriate
specialist. This created something of a trial and error process
involving persons with very special needs as they did not actually see
the modifications until the sale was completed. The industry has since
evolved. Currently, motor vehicle manufacturers and vehicle "alterers"
work in tandem to produce standardized mobility vehicle models -- and
OEM franchised dealers and dealers specializing in mobility vehicles
cooperate in a manner that allows consumers to examine "completed"
mobility vehicles up front and first hand - greatly benefitting
purchasers with disabilities and their families.


Generally, the display, demonstration and ultimate sale of these
specialized vehicles throughout the country consist of the following
steps. Large mobility vehicle alterers modify new OEM vehicles for
ingress, transportation, and egress of wheelchair and scooter users.
These altered/modified vehicles are generally owned by OEM-franchised
dealers before and after the vehicles are converted into mobility
vehicles by the mobility vehicle alterer. NYS-located mobility dealers
then order the new mobility vehicles from the OEM-franchised dealer,
so the vehicles can be displayed, advertised, stored and demonstrated
on the mobility dealer's showroom floors. People with disabilities
visit the mobility dealers to actually view the displayed new mobility
vehicles, take a test drive, and learn how the vehicle can be further
modified to best accommodate the individual's specific disability.

Ultimately, the consumer with the disability will purchase the base
vehicle from the OEM-franchised dealer, or an alterer holding proper
title to the vehicle, and will purchase the mobility modifications
from the mobility dealer. The underlying vehicle continues to be
warranted by the original equipment manufacturer and the modifications
are warranted by the alterer.

This system has proven uniformly beneficial; however, under the
Vehicle and Traffic Law, the mobility dealers are currently classified
as "used car dealers". However, due to the fact that they are
displaying new vehicles (albeit modified) in their showrooms for
demonstration purposes, they are technically in violation of § 415 of
the Arm. This legislation allows mobility dealers to become fully
compliant with New York motor vehicle dealer law while maintaining
their specialized and limited area of expertise and unique
relationship with their customers. The sophisticated relationships
between new car manufacturers, alterers, OEM franchised dealers, and
mobility dealers have resulted in substantial benefits in quality,
reliability and affordability for persons with disabilities. The
modifications contained in this legislation will allow the benefits to
the disabled community and their families continue and grow.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: New bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None

EFFECTIVE DATE: This act shall take effect on th6 thirtieth day after
which it has become law
